title: Belgium – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Customs SEED+ Maintenance, Upgrade and Risk Management Support
description: Maintenance, support and upgrade of Customs SEED+ and related customs digital systems. Customs SEED+ is a digital platform supporting the systematic electronic exchange of customs data and pre-arrival information between CEFTA customs administrations, and between CEFTA and participating EU Member States through the Green Lanes initiative. The platform supports data exchange, risk management, trade facilitation, monitoring of crossing point performance, and the implementation of common customs cooperation tools. The contract will also support interoperability with local customs systems and related CEFTA systems, gradual alignment with the new Union Customs Code framework and related EU customs data exchange requirements, as well as further development of customs risk management functionalities and support for the recognition of customs controls, including common risk profiles, rapid customs alerts, inspection report data exchange, AEO-related functionalities, statistics and reporting, where relevant.

title: U009--FY27 ACPE Accreditation & Dues (Chaplain Service)
description: Special Notice Special Notice Page 3 of 3 Special Notice *= Required Field Special Notice Page 1 of 3 The Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office (NCO) 6, intends to award a sole-source purchase order to the Association for Clinical Pastoral Education, Inc. (ACPE), for accreditation, consultation, and educational support services for the Chaplain Service Office at the Durham VA Health Care System in Durham, North Carolina. ACPE accreditation enables the Durham VA Health Care System to provide accredited Clinical Pastoral Education (CPE) to residents and students. Maintaining ACPE accreditation supports the facility s continued operation of its accredited CPE program and, as applicable, its eligibility to request resident training stipends through the Department of Veterans Affairs Office of Academic Affiliations (OAA). The CPE program provides education and supervised clinical training that support the delivery of spiritual care to Veterans. The required services include: Maintaining the Durham VA Health Care System s ACPE accreditation during the period of performance; Providing consultation regarding compliance with applicable ACPE accreditation standards and requirements; Providing ongoing consultation concerning the education and training of CPE residents and students; Providing consultation and support related to the certification and continuing education of ACPE Certified Educators; and Providing access to applicable ACPE accreditation, educational, and professional-development resources included within the accreditation arrangement. ACPE is the only reasonably available source for the required ACPE accreditation and ACPE-specific accreditation consultation. The requirement cannot be satisfied by a general training provider or another accreditation organization because such an organization would not provide ACPE accreditation, consultation regarding ACPE standards, or ACPE-related educator-certification support. Substitution of another source would not maintain the required ACPE accreditation or provide the same accreditation, standards, certification, and program-support functions. The period of performance will be one 12-month period beginning November 1, 2026, and ending October 31, 2027. The Government has determined that only one source is reasonably available to provide the required services and has documented the basis for that determination in accordance with FAR 12.102(a). The acquisition will be conducted using the applicable simplified procedures for commercial services under FAR 12.201-1. This special notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotations. No solicitation documents are available, and telephone requests will not be accepted. However, any business that believes it can provide the complete requirement may submit a written capability statement. The response must include sufficient information and supporting documentation to demonstrate the firm s ability to meet all requirements described above, including authorization to provide ACPE accreditation and related ACPE-specific services. Responses will be considered by the Government; however, the Government retains sole discretion to determine whether to compete the proposed acquisition based on the responses received. title: DA01--FY 27 NYH ISCV DATA RECOVERY SERVICES - 1 YEAR ONLY
description: Sources Sought Notice Sources Sought Notice Page 5 of 5 *= Required Field Sources Sought Notice Page 1 of 5 This notice is for the purpose of identifying parties having an interest in and the resources to support this requirement for: Philips ISCV Radiographic DICOM Data Recovery Services needed for the VA New York Harbor Healthcare System, Manhattan Campus located at 423 E 23rd Street New York, NY 10010. Background VA New York Harbor Healthcare System has two critical NetGear ReadyNAS 3220 storage systems used to house all Philips ISCV Radiographic DICOM studies from 2007 2020. The primary NAS, XLBACKUP1, contained the active historical repository of patient studies, while XLARCHIVE served as an exact mirror backup. Both systems have experienced hardware failure resulting in complete RAID volume loss. What happened: Both NETGEAR ReadyNAS 3220 systems failed, resulting in loss of both RAID6 volumes. Hardware details: 2× NETGEAR ReadyNAS 3220 NAS systems 12 disks per NAS, 12 disks per volume Disk type: SATA 2.0 TB, model WD20000FYYZ 01UL1B1 RAID configuration: RAID 6 Objectives & Scope The Manhattan VA NYHHS requires professional forensic data recovery services to restore patient Radiographic DICOM studies (Year 2007 Year 2020) lost due to the RAID volume failures described above. The vendor's work is divided into custody/handling, recovery, and secure destruction obligations as follows: Custody, Imaging & Recovery Pick up or receive labeled drives from VA. Every individual who handles or works on the drives must complete and sign a VA Chain of Custody form. Forensically image all original NAS disks (no intrusive work on originals, unless physical repair of a disk is necessary to enable imaging). All accessible DICOM studies (Year 2007 Year 2020) are restored. Metadata and directory structure are intact and properly associated with studies. Delivery & Data Destruction Provide recovered datasets on externally accessible media. Ensure recovered datasets can be successfully migrated into AGFA Radiology PACS. Upon written confirmation from the VA to be provided within 14 business days of delivery of the recovered data and files that the recovered data and files have been reviewed and accepted, destroy all VA data, including but not limited to any cloned disk images, extracted information, metadata, temporary processing files, logs, or partial RAID reconstructions created during the recovery process. Provide the VA with a Certificate of Destruction, signed by an authorized compliance officer, confirming that all VA data from internal systems, temporary storage, cloned disk images, and any other media has been securely purged and irreversibly destroyed. Item/Quantity Description Item Description Qty 1 Return of all 24 original disks 24 disks 2 Recovery of all patient studies (Year 2007 Year 2020) on portable media 1 Period of Performance The estimated date of period of performance will begin around December 1st, 2026 and end on January 31st, 2027. The procurement will be conducted under FAR Part 12 Part 12 - Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. The NAICS code is 541512, and the size standard is $34 million. There is no solicitation at this time. This request for capability information does not constitute a request for proposals; submission of any information in response to this market survey is purely voluntary; the government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred. Responses to this announcement will be used to determine the market for this service and whether sufficient interest exists to set the procurement aside. Responses to this notice shall be submitted via e-mail to tevia.mastykarz@va.gov by October 23rd, 2026. Telephone replies will not be honored. If your organization has the interest and capability to perform these services, please provide the following information: 1) Organization name, address, email address, website address, telephone number, and size and type of ownership for the organization; and 2) A tailored capability statement addressing the particulars of this effort, with appropriate documentation supporting claims of capability. 3) Responses shall confirm a clean-room facility: The contractor must have and maintain a current clean-room Class-10 (ISO 4) certification for all physical drive disassembly, head-swap, or platter-level recovery work. title: Sizing Technology Pilot
description: **16 October 2026 - Amendment 1 - The purpose of this amendment is to: 1. Update the Call for Solutions document. Updates are highlighted in yellow. 2. Provide Government responses to industry questions. 3. Extend the solution brief submission deadline. The solicitation closing date is hereby extended from 20 October 2026 at 10:00 AM ET to 23 October 2026 at 10:00 AM ET. Please see the Attachments section documents titled "Attachment 1 - CFS HQDA-G-4_26_01 Sizing Technology Pilot R1 101626" and "Attachment 2 - CFS_Sizing Technology Pilot_QandA 101626" for updates.** Sizing Technology Pilot This Call for Solutions (CFS) is issued under the Army Open Solicitation (AOS) W9128Z-25-S-A002. The Army Contracting Command-Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG) on behalf of the Headquarters Department of the Army (HQDA), G-4, is seeking innovative solutions capable of accurately capturing both body and foot measurements using automated, non-contact methods and translating those measurements into recommended standard Army uniform and footwear sizes. The Army faces a significant challenge in accurately and efficiently outfitting personnel throughout their careers. The current reliance on manual tape measurements at accession points creates logistical bottlenecks, high rates of uniform/boot returns, and provides no mechanism for capturing changes to a Soldier's sizing data over time. The objective of this CFS is to identify and evaluate mature commercial technologies for a Sizing Technology Pilot. The Call for Solutions document titled �Attachment 1 - CFS HQDA-G-4_26_01 Sizing Technology Pilot� outlining the full problem statement, required and desired solution attributes, submission requirements, and evaluation phases/criteria, can be found in the "Attachments" section below. The deadline to submit questions for this CFS is 13 October 2026 at 10:00 AM ET. All questions must be submitted via email to the POCs listed in this notice with the following subject line: "CFS HQDA-G-4_26_01 Sizing Technology Pilot" The Army Open Solicitation (AOS) that this Call for Solutions is associated with can be found at the following link: https://sam.gov/opp/f192de32276644418358784eb8427ee2/view Please review the AOS posting and associated attachments, in addition to the attachments to this Call for further information on how the AOS is structured.

title: EDC Branded Merchandise Platform
description: EDC is seeking a solution to provide and operate a secure, customizable online Branded Merchandise platform. The platform must allow authorized EDC employees to order approved Branded Merchandise through a centralized online storefront. EDC’s primary objective for this requirement is to support Business Orders for approved Branded Merchandise. EDC is seeking a single vendor of record for the Branded Merchandise program, responsible for end-to-end service delivery on EDC’s behalf, including sourcing, storage, inventory management, fulfillment, and delivery. Where feasible, priority should be given to Canadian-made and Canadian-supplied products. The Preferred Proponent will manage the full lifecycle of Branded Merchandise, including product sourcing, brand compliance, warehousing, pick-and-pack services, fulfillment, and domestic and international shipping. The Proponent must also provide governance and administrative capabilities, such as approvals, budget controls, and reporting. This engagement will help EDC centralize Branded Merchandise management, improve operational efficiency, maintain brand consistency, increase access to approved items, and monitor and control costs across the organization more effectively. EDC aims to achieve the following business objectives: Centralize the management of Branded Merchandise across EDC Improve operational efficiency and cost control Ensure consistent governance and brand application across Branded Merchandise Enable self-service ordering with appropriate governance Provide greater access to all EDC and employees to purchased Branded Merchandise for Business Orders and Personal Purchases Support domestic and international delivery needs Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

title: Expression of Interest for National Curriculum - Oracy Framework Expert Sector Panel
description: The Department for Education (DfE) is seeking to appoint, via an expression of interest (EOI), expert panel members to support the development of the Primary Oracy Framework. Although this is a primary framework, this document will include secondary content and may require secondary expertise. The panel members will work with the lead drafter and DfE to produce a document that provides non-statutory guidance to support the effective teaching of oracy in schools. Panel members will have strong theoretical oracy-expertise and/or extensive experience of delivering oracy across the curriculum, in programmes for schools and CPD for teachers and leaders in different education settings. The role of panel member will include: i. providing expertise and experience to support the development of the framework, including on accuracy of content and deliverability of the content. ii. drafting sections/chapters of the framework and/or making contributions to sections/chapters. iii. attending regular meetings with the DfE & lead drafter to contribute to discussions on the scope and content of the document. The panel will provide advice and guidance and reach a consensus on the issues discussed. iv. advising on evidence and examples of best practice in England and internationally. v. providing regular reviews of content and comment on different iterations of the draft framework. vi. commenting on options for a sustainable approach to the delivery of the Primary-Oracy-Framework, taking account of relevant good practice and innovation from the wider sector. vii. supporting the launch of the Primary Oracy Framework, including using their own networks where appropriate. All panel members will operate on a pro-bono basis. However, where travel expenses are incurred by panel members for in-person meetings, the DfE will reimburse panel members. Governance and Quality Assurance The Department will appoint a lead drafter to develop and drafter the Primary Oracy Framework. This will be a pro-bono agreement, & no fees or commercial consideration will be paid by the Department under this agreement. To support transparency and independent challenge, an Expert Panel will be established through an open Expression of Interest process. How to Apply Applicants must review & comply with the requirements, eligibility criteria, and detailed application instructions set out in the attached documentation. Applications should include only the information and supporting evidence specifically requested within the application documents. Failure to follow the application instructions or provide the required information may result in the application not being considered. To be considered, applicants must: 1. Review attached Specification and supporting documents; 2. Complete the official EOI Application Form provided with this opportunity; 3. Submit the completed Application Form (and any requested supporting information) to oracy.FRAMEWORK@education.gov.uk by 4pm 23-10-26

title: Civilian Armored Vehicle Manufacturers
description: PURPOSE This Sources Sought Notice seeks to identify potential vendors that specialize in civilian armored vehicles. The Government will only accept responses from firms that perform the actual armoring work from start to finish. Responses from brokers or intermediaries will not be accepted. MANUFACTURING LOCATION REQUIREMENT All vehicle armoring work under any resultant contract shall be performed at facilities located in the United States. The resultant contract will not allow the Contractor to perform or subcontract any armoring work to facilities located in countries subject to U.S. sanctions or export control restrictions. ANTICIPATED CONTRACT DETAILS Contract Type: Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Period of Performance: One (1) year base period plus nine (9) twelve-month option periods INFORMATION REQUESTED Interested parties should provide the following information in their response: 1. Company Information a. Company name b. Company address c. Point of contact (POC) name, phone number, and email address d. DUNS number (or UEI if transitioned) 2. Small Business Status a. Indicate whether your company is a small business under NAICS code 336211 b. If applicable, list the socioeconomic category in which your company belongs (e.g., 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB) 3. SAM Registration a. Confirm that your company is registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) i. Provide SAM UEI number 4. Capability Statement (20-page maximum), focusing on your firm's ability to armor various types of passenger vehicles: a. Armoring Experience � Provide details of vehicle armoring experience in the private and/or public sectors for the previous 10 years, including: i. Types of vehicles armored; make, model, and model year going back no further than 10 years. ii. Example use cases of past vehicles armored (e.g., cargo transport, VIP protection). iii. Ballistic and blast protection levels achieved for standards such as NIJ, VPAM, STANAG, etc., and any non-standard protection requirements met. iv. Fabrication capability for opaque armor materials, and types and thicknesses of materials used in previous armored vehicles. v. Client references (if releasable). b. Contract Volume and Track Record i. Total dollar value of vehicle armoring contracts/orders performed annually over the past 3 years. ii. Largest single order (by vehicle quantity and dollar value) completed within a 12-month period. c. Manufacturing Capabilities i. Location(s) of manufacturing facility/facilities. ii. Any subcontractors used in vehicle production. iii. Production capacity in vehicles per year. iv. Current production lead time, from contract/order award to delivery, for a single vehicle and for a batch order (e.g., 10, 25, 50 vehicles). v. Surge capacity: ability to increase production temporarily to meet urgent Government requirements, and associated timelines. vi. Quality certifications (e.g., ISO, industry-specific certifications). 5. Facility Security Clearances a. Details regarding current and/or past facility security clearances (e.g., FCL level and expiration date) 6. GSA Schedule (if applicable) a. GSA Schedule number b. Period of performance 7. Acquisition Strategy and Contract Structure Feedback a. Does your firm have experience performing under an IDIQ contract with multiple 12-month option periods? If so, please describe. b. Would your firm be able to compete effectively if this requirement is set aside for small business, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, or WOSB concerns? Please explain any concerns with a small business set-aside. c. Based on your knowledge of the industry, are you aware of at least two other capable, responsible small businesses that could perform this requirement? (This helps the Government assess set-aside feasibility under the Rule of Two.) d. Would your firm prefer or recommend a single-award IDIQ or a multiple-award IDIQ for this requirement? Please explain the rationale. e. Do you have experience with, or a preference for, Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) task/delivery orders versus other pricing arrangements (e.g., FFP with economic price adjustment) for this type of work, given potential material cost volatility (e.g., steel, ballistic glass, composites)? f. What is a reasonable Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost range per vehicle for common armoring configurations (e.g., B4/B6 level sedan, B7 level SUV), if you are able to share this for planning purposes? g. Are there minimum order quantities or dollar thresholds your firm would require to make individual task orders economically viable? h. What is your firm's standard warranty period and terms for armoring work performed, including coverage for parts, labor, and any workmanship defects? i. Is your firm capable of providing warranty support at U.S. Department of State posts located overseas? If so, please describe how this support would be delivered, including: Delivery method � e.g., dispatch of traveling technicians from the U.S. or a regional hub, use of vetted local subcontractors/service partners, or a combination of both; Coordination with post � how your firm would coordinate with the post's General Services Office (GSO) or Facilities Management team to schedule access, obtain necessary country clearances, and comply with local security and customs requirements; Response times � anticipated timeframes for initial response and on-site arrival, accounting for post location (e.g., high-threat vs. standard posts) and regional logistics; Parts and logistics � how replacement parts or materials would be sourced and shipped to the post, including any customs, or import/export control considerations; and Limitations � any posts, regions, or security environments where your firm would be unable to provide direct warranty service, and what alternative arrangements (e.g., remote technical support, depot-level repair) would apply in those cases. j. Does your firm have bonding capacity sufficient to support a multi-year IDIQ of this size? If comfortable sharing, please indicate your bonding capacity or capacity range. k. Would your firm be interested in, or already positioned for, teaming or subcontracting arrangements with other firms to meet the full scope of this requirement? l. Are there any customer-furnished vehicle chassis considerations (e.g., Government-furnished base vehicles vs. contractor-procured) that would affect your proposed approach or pricing? m. Do you foresee any barriers (e.g., export control licensing, material sourcing, facility capacity) that could limit competition or timely performance under this requirement? SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Deadline: Responses must be received no later than 11:00 AM EST on October 23, 2026. Submission Method: All responses, including attachments and any questions regarding this Notice, should be submitted electronically to: Maria Anguiano: anguianom@state.gov Wanda I. Cruz: cruzwi@state.gov Subject Line: Sources Sought Response � Motor Vehicle Body Manufacturing

title: JTRS Ground Adaptor Kit
description: ADM(MAT), on behalf of the RCAF, has identified a requirement to procure commercially available power supplies, rack-mount cooling equipment, and factory-terminated cabling to support the operation of JTRS Platform I radios in fixed-site Link 16 operational and training environments. The purpose of this procurement is to enable JTRS Platform I radios to operate outside pre-integrated rack solutions by providing the necessary ancillary hardware for power distribution, thermal management, and external connectivity, without including installation, system integration, testing, or certification. JTRS Platform I radios require external DC power conversion, forced-air cooling capable of supporting both the radio and its associated power supply in a single 19-inch rack, and standardized power, data/control, and human-machine interface cabling manufactured in accordance with recognized military and aerospace construction practices. Some required cable assemblies rely on controlled U.S. Government interface specifications, limiting eligible suppliers to those with existing authorization. The procurement also includes external rack-mountable DC power supplies capable of delivering nominal 280 VDC at continuous duty and rack-compatible multi-fan cooling assemblies rated for sustained high-power transmission. Deliverables consist of 20 DC power supply units, 20 rack-mount cooling trays, and 20 complete sets of factory-terminated power, data/control, timing, and HMIG cables as defined in the specification. To be delivered to Unit #3 1941 Robertson Road Bells Corners, Nepean Ottawa ON K2H 5B7.

title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source to RVET Operating LLC for Job Fair Participation
description: The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Office of Marine and Aviation Operations (OMAO), using the procedures set forth in RFO Part 12, intends to negotiate on a sole source basis with RVET Operating, LLC. located at 3012 River Reach, Williamsburg, VA 23185 for a firm-fixed price purchase order to have booths at job fairs hosted by RVET Operating. Award is anticipated to occur by November 13, 2026. OMAO requires wage mariners to crew NOAA�s research and survey vessels alongside the NOAA Commissioned Officer Corps. OMAO requires a large variety of a wage mariner workforce, including masters, mates, engineers, deckhands, and stewards. To achieve this, OMAO conducts targeted outreach through a variety of methods, including attendance at national recruiting events such as job and career fairs. OMAO seeks to increase its efforts to reach out to military veterans, to include transitioning or soon to be separated military veterans when pursuing opportunities to fill current OMAO wage mariner requirements. Veterans are often uniquely familiar with work onboard a ship such as one of NOAA�s vessels. OMAO will require a partner who has access to potential employees at their current military service locations, or within the immediate vicinity of Department of Defense installations. RVET Operating offers events on military installations, city-based, virtual, and private in-person as part of its services which are unavailable from any other source. RVET Operating is the only company contracted by the US Army�s Human Resources Command and the Department of Labor for veteran hiring. RVET Operating hosts more than 100 job fairs annually and in order to have a booth at an RVET Operating event OMAO must contract with RVET Operating. No other company has the authority to grant booth access to an event operated by RVET Operating. The North American Industry Classification System Code (NAICS) is 561311, Employment Placement Agencies which has a size standard of $34M. This requirement will be issued as a small business set-aside. This presolicitation notice does not constitute a solicitation - a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), or an Invitation for Bid (IFB) - and it does not restrict the Government in any way regarding its ultimate acquisition approach. However, if any other interested party believes that it can meet the requirements, it may submit a statement of capabilities, which if timely received, will be considered by NOAA. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed requirement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement in the future. Evidence must be provided of ability to provide the required services. The capability statement and any other information furnished must be in writing and must contain material in sufficient detail to allow NOAA to determine if the party can meet all of the requirements. Capability statements and related materials must be e-mailed to Contract Specialist Elizabeth Eichelberger at Elizabeth.Eichelberger@noaa.gov within 15 days of the posting of this notice.

title: INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE - FLASHPOINT INTELLIGENCE CAPABILITIES AND SERVICES
description: Agency U.S. Department of the Treasury Departmental Offices & Enterprise Procurement Branch Treasury Common Services Center Acquisition Services Action Notice of Intent to Award a Sole Source Firm Fixed Price Contract Description The U.S. Department of the Treasury, Departmental Offices & Enterprise Procurement Branch, Treasury Common Services Center - Acquisition Services, intends to award a sole source contract to Thundercat Technologies for a subscription to a commercial-off-the-shelf specialized threat intelligence tool to support the defense and operational resilience of the Nation's critical financial infrastructure for the Treasury�s Office of The Office of Cybersecurity and Critical Infrastructure Protection (OCCIP). This requirement is for timely, relevant, and actionable intelligence from primary-source, open-source, deep-web, dark-web, illicit-marketplace, messaging, and geospatial sources. The solution must support financial fraud detection and loss tracking, cyber threat actor tracking, vulnerability exploitation contextualization, cyber and physical incident monitoring, geospatial situational awareness, investigations, alerting, and informed decision-making through Flashpoint Ignite. The Government has determined that Thundercat Technologies is the only source capable of meeting the Government's requirements because Thundercat developed and owns the propriety and patented hardware, software, and algorithms that are used in the required products and support the services specifically required for this acquisition. The anticipated award is for a base period of 12-months, with four (4) option period(s). Interested Sources This notice is not a solicitation or a request for competitive quotations or proposals. However, responsible sources that believe they can provide the required supplies or services may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to meet the Government's requirements. Capability statements must include sufficient technical information to determine whether the interested party can satisfy the Government's requirement without substantial duplication of cost or unacceptable delays. Responses shall include: 1. Company name and address; 2. Size of company (number of personnel, total revenue, ownership, parent corporation, etc.); 3. Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) 4. Please identify type of �ordering� contract (e.g., GSA Multiple Award Schedule, GSA Professional Service Schedule, etc.). Responses received by the specified deadline will be evaluated solely to determine whether a competitive procurement should be conducted. Response Deadline Responses must be received no later than 12:00PM EDT on October 23, 2026. Submit responses electronically to: Contracting Officer: Angela C. Gallo Email: angela.gallo@treasury.gov Disclaimer This notice is for informational purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with preparing or submitting a response. description: This requirement is for membership in The Acoustical Society of America (ASA). NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD SINGLE SOURCE: The NAICS Code is 813920 � Professional Organizations. The Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) Enterprise Strategies and Initiatives Contracting Division (RMZ), located at Wright-Patterson AFB, Ohio, intends to award a sole source purchase order as authorized by RFO 12.102(a) to The Acoustical Society of America (ASA). This Notice of Intent is NOT a request for competitive quotes or proposals. A determination by the Government for the competition of this requirement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. All responsible sources or authorized distributors may submit a capability statement that meets all the requirements in the attached Minimum Requirements Document (MRD) dated 05 August 2026, quotation, or exception to the intent to purchase on a sole source basis, which shall be considered by the Government via e-mail to Mr. Christof Olp-Weakland at christopher.olp-weakland@us.af.mil no later than Friday 23 October 2026 at 12:00pm Eastern Time. Only responses received by this date will be considered. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Be advised that all correspondence sent via e-mail shall contain a subject line that reads �Notice of Intent to Award SS � Acoustical Society�. title: Prototype development for Battlefield Wound Infection Prevention and Treatment (BWI P&T) Barrier Combination
description: This RPP is being issued by the Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA), in support of the Defense Health Agency�s Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Medical Products (MP) Warfighter Protection (WPAC) & Acute Care Program Management Office (PMO) Care located in Frederick, Maryland at Fort Detrick. The Warfighter Protection and Acute Care Project Management Office (WPAC PMO) has a requirement for the development of a Barrier Combination product. The Barrier Combination product is defined as being composed of both a physical barrier to protect a wound and an antibacterial and/or antifungal activity released from the barrier to prevent the spread of organisms and avoid systemic infections. This RPP will result in one award to develop the Battlefield Wound Infection Prevention and Treatment (BWI P&T) Barrier Combination (BC) prototype product. The final product MUST be a combination wound treatment that includes a barrier component that is either infused or impregnated with antimicrobial and/or antifungal properties and have U.S. Food Drug Administration (FDA) approval (or clearance). The award, as a result of this RPP, will be awarded under the authority of prototype Other Transaction Authority (pOTA) 10 U.S.C. 4022.

title: Intent to Sole Source - Medical/Scientific Instruments for the Department of Transfusion Medicine, NIH Clinical Center
description: This is a Notice of Intent, not a request for proposal. The National Institute of Health, Clinical Center (NIH-CC) intends to negotiate on an other than full and open competition basis with the following vendor: Fisher Scientific. Acquisition Description: The NIH Clinical Center, Department of Transfusion Medicine (DTM), Infectious Diseases Section requires acquisition of a 1) Real-Time PCR System, 2) an Automated Nucleic Acid Extractor and 3) a microvolume spectrophotometer to support clinical research and the development, optimization, and validation of diagnostic assays for hepatitis viruses and other transfusion-transmitted pathogens. The required system must support generation of high-quality quantification data from clinical specimens, including viral RNA/DNA and host-derived nucleic acids. The instrument must enable applications such as targeted genome amplification, work with a wider dynamic detection range, support the library prep for viral genome sequencing, and assay development workflows necessary for evaluating test performance and refining diagnostic methods prior to implementation in a clinical testing environment. The system must meet the following functional and operational requirements: High data accuracy and reproducibility to ensure reliable detection of viral variants and evaluation of assay performance; Low- to moderate-throughput capability appropriate for assay development, pilot studies, and validation activities involving smaller sample sets; Rapid turnaround times to support iterative testing and optimization of clinical assays; Flexible run configurations that allow efficient processing of varying sample volumes without excess capacity; Cost-efficient operation, including the ability to minimize per-run and per-sample costs for pathogen detection; Integrated and streamlined workflows, including nucleic acid extraction, amplification, quantification and data analysis within a platform from the same vendor to reduce complexity and variability; Ease of use and standardized operation, supporting reproducibility and implementation in a clinical laboratory environment; Compatibility with established nucleic acid preparation and amplification methods and existing laboratory workflows. The flexibility to be using the systems in a CLIA certified environment. The statutory authority for this sole source requirement is 41 U.S.C. 253(c) (1) as implemented by FAR 6.302-1 only one responsible source and no other supply of service will satisfy agency requirements. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. All responsible sources that could provide the required may submit a capability statement that will be considered by email (subject line to reference NOI-OLAO-CC-27-000121) by 12:00 PM eastern standard time on 10/23/2026 to: valerie.gregorio@nih.gov. All responses received by the closing date of this synopsis will be considered by the Government. A determination not to compete this requirement, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government.

description: W912EE - THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE AND SHOULD NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A SOLICITATION ANNOUNCEMENT. THE SUBMISSION OF THIS INFORMATION IS FOR PLANNING PURPOSES ONLY. IT IS NOT TO BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT TO PROCURE ANY SERVICES, AND THE VICKSBURG DISTRICT DOES NOT INTEND TO AWARD A CONTRACT ON THE BASIS OF THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Vicksburg District (MVK) is conducting market research to determine the availability of a hydraulic-cutterhead dredge, not less than 18-inches in diameter. For the purposes of this announcement MVK is seeking to identify the availability of an (18� or larger dredge) for potential riverine dredging of the Mississippi River Harbors and/or lock approaches of the JBJ Waterway (Red River) within the MVK area of responsibility. A market survey is being conducted to determine if there are a reasonable number of firms, large or small businesses, capable of mobilizing and interested in performing the required work in the required locations. A decision as to whether the work will be set-aside for specific socio-economic category businesses is pending. We would like to hear from large business, small businesses, small disadvantaged businesses, HUBZONE small businesses, woman-owned small businesses, or service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses. In any case, if you are interested in this work, please respond accordingly. Responses to this sources-sought announcement will be used by the Government to make appropriate acquisition decisions. The NAICS Code for this acquisition is 237990 � Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction � Dredging and Surface Cleanup Activities with a size standard of $37 million. This Sources Sought Synopsis shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government, nor will any reimbursement be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this request or any follow up information requests. NO SOLICITATION IS CURRENTLY AVAILABLE. BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: For the purpose of market research, USACE MVK will be utilizing this request for information to determine the availability of sources capable of providing the services required as well as the acquisition approach best suited for this project. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Vicksburg District (MVK) is planning for the solicitation & award of contracts for dredging at Mississippi River Ports and Harbors and for dredging on the JBJ Waterway. Contractors would be required to furnish all plant, labor, materials, and equipment necessary for performing construction and maintenance dredging. The material to be dredged will consist of sand, gravel, loose rock, silt, mud and clay; and in certain localities stumps, roots, logs, riprap, driftwood, sunken objects, and miscellaneous debris may be encountered. The dredge must be equipped with suitable pump impellers and cutters to efficiently handle these varying materials on pipeline lengths up to 6,500 feet. Dredges should be available immediately, and contractors should have adequate bonding capability. RESPONSE FORMAT: Responses shall not exceed five (5) pages in total, inclusive of all offeror attachments. A one (1) page executive summary shall not be considered part of the total page limit. The Capability Statement shall be comprised of the below information: 1. Brief History of the company. 2. Experience in delivering same or similar services/supplies. This section shall demonstrate the offer's experience and ability to provide skilled personnel and manage requirements that are the same or similar to those addressed in the project description or PWS. 3. List of current or previous contracts: The offeror shall provide contract title, contract number, period of performance, dollar amount, and description of work performed on up to five Government contracts. List should be limited to work performed within the last five years and include reference name, email, and phone number. 4. General information: a. Company name, address, point of contact, telephone number, and e-mail address. b. CAGE Code/UEI Number c. NAICS (list all NAICS under which your firm is registered) d. Offeror's business size to include designation as Certified Small Businesses, 8(a) contractors, HUBZone Certified Small Business Concerns, Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses, and Women-Owned Small For 8(a) Contractors, please include anticipated graduation date from the 8(a) Program. e. Identification of Joint Venture, if applicable (Business Name, Business Size and Cage Code of JV). 5. Offeror's bonding capability (construction bonding level per contract and aggregate construction bonding level, both expressed in dollars). Interested contractors shall submit their responses by e-mail only. Responses should be submitted as a single PDF document (not scanned). Hard copies will not be accepted. Responses to this notice are due no later than 12:00 PM Central Daylight Time on Friday, October 23, 2026, via e-mail to the primary point of contact listed Andrew McCaskill at andrew.mccaskill@usace.army.mil.

title: Construction of Chilled Water Plant and Site Utility Upgrades at VA Medical Center in West Haven, CT
description: The scope of the chilled water plant replacement consists of the demolition of the existing chilled water plant (building 16a) and construction of a new multi-story chilled water plant to include chillers, cooling towers, pumps, and all associated mechanical and electrical equipment. Due to the close proximity of the existing fuel tank farm adjacent to the existing chilled water plant, a new fuel tank farm will need to be constructed as part of the project, which primarily serves the central boiler plant, requiring close coordination with the medical center and ongoing related projects.The scope of the site utility upgrades consists of the replacement and upgrade of the existing fire protection water main and the domestic water main from Campbell Avenue to Building 15. Site utility upgrades also include providing utility main loops of chilled water supply and return, steam supply, condensate return, domestic water supply, and fire protection water supply which will originate from the new chilled water plant and back-feed to Building 1. The work also includes the installation of redundant electrical feeder from the utility demarcation point to Building 19 and coordination with the local electrical utility provider to provide further electrical redundancy offsite as well. In addition, new water storage tanks will be constructed. This project involves civil/site, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, structural, geotechnical, and architectural disciplines. The project must also comply with the DVAs Physical Security Resiliency Design Requirements (PSRDM). It is expected that the chilled water plant will be constructed to meet USGBC LEED Silver certification. The work is located adjacent to and within an active Medical Center campus which will be operational at all times. Impact to on-going operations must be kept to a minimum and carefully coordinated with the Contracting Officer and VAMC staff. In addition, the work area is constrained due to the active medical center operations which will limit laydown and storage areas during construction.

title: Construction of Chilled Water Plant and Site Utility Upgrades at VA Medical Center in West Haven, CT
description: The scope of the chilled water plant replacement consists of the demolition of the existing chilled water plant (building 16a) and construction of a new multi-story chilled water plant to include chillers, cooling towers, pumps, and all associated mechanical and electrical equipment. Due to the close proximity of the existing fuel tank farm adjacent to the existing chilled water plant, a new fuel tank farm will need to be constructed as part of the project, which primarily serves the central boiler plant, requiring close coordination with the medical center and ongoing related projects.The scope of the site utility upgrades consists of the replacement and upgrade of the existing fire protection water main and the domestic water main from Campbell Avenue to Building 15. Site utility upgrades also include providing utility main loops of chilled water supply and return, steam supply, condensate return, domestic water supply, and fire protection water supply which will originate from the new chilled water plant and back-feed to Building 1. The work also includes the installation of redundant electrical feeder from the utility demarcation point to Building 19 and coordination with the local electrical utility provider to provide further electrical redundancy offsite as well. In addition, new water storage tanks will be constructed. This project involves civil/site, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, structural, geotechnical, and architectural disciplines. The project must also comply with the DVAs Physical Security Resiliency Design Requirements (PSRDM). It is expected that the chilled water plant will be constructed to meet USGBC LEED Silver certification. The work is located adjacent to and within an active Medical Center campus which will be operational at all times. Impact to on-going operations must be kept to a minimum and carefully coordinated with the Contracting Officer and VAMC staff. In addition, the work area is constrained due to the active medical center operations which will limit laydown and storage areas during construction.

title: Lease of One Cutterhead, Hydraulic Pipeline Dredge (Not Less Than 18-Inch Diameter), Fully Operated with Attendant Plant and Personnel, and with a Draft not to Exceed 9 Feet, for Construction and Maintenance Dredging within the Vicksburg District
description: W912EE - THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE AND SHOULD NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A SOLICITATION ANNOUNCEMENT. THE SUBMISSION OF THIS INFORMATION IS FOR PLANNING PURPOSES ONLY. IT IS NOT TO BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT TO PROCURE ANY SERVICES, AND THE VICKSBURG DISTRICT DOES NOT INTEND TO AWARD A CONTRACT ON THE BASIS OF THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Vicksburg District (MVK) is conducting market research to determine the availability of a hydraulic-cutterhead dredge, not less than 18-inches in diameter. For the purposes of this announcement MVK is seeking to identify the availability of an (18� or larger dredge) for potential riverine dredging of the Mississippi River Harbors and/or lock approaches of the JBJ Waterway (Red River) within the MVK area of responsibility. A market survey is being conducted to determine if there are a reasonable number of firms, large or small businesses, capable of mobilizing and interested in performing the required work in the required locations. A decision as to whether the work will be set-aside for specific socio-economic category businesses is pending. We would like to hear from large business, small businesses, small disadvantaged businesses, HUBZONE small businesses, woman-owned small businesses, or service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses. In any case, if you are interested in this work, please respond accordingly. Responses to this sources-sought announcement will be used by the Government to make appropriate acquisition decisions. The NAICS Code for this acquisition is 237990 � Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction � Dredging and Surface Cleanup Activities with a size standard of $37 million. This Sources Sought Notice shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government, nor will any reimbursement be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this request or any follow up information requests. NO SOLICITATION IS CURRENTLY AVAILABLE. BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: For the purpose of market research, USACE MVK will be utilizing this request for information to determine the availability of sources capable of providing the services required as well as the acquisition approach best suited for this project. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Vicksburg District (MVK) is planning for the solicitation & award of contracts for dredging at Mississippi River Ports and Harbors and for dredging on the JBJ Waterway. Contractors would be required to furnish all plant, labor, materials, and equipment necessary for performing construction and maintenance dredging. The material to be dredged will consist of sand, gravel, loose rock, silt, mud and clay; and in certain localities stumps, roots, logs, riprap, driftwood, sunken objects, and miscellaneous debris may be encountered. The dredge must be equipped with suitable pump impellers and cutters to efficiently handle these varying materials on pipeline lengths up to 6,500 feet. Dredges should be available immediately, and contractors should have adequate bonding capability. RESPONSE FORMAT: Responses shall not exceed five (5) pages in total, inclusive of all offeror attachments. A one (1) page executive summary shall not be considered part of the total page limit. The Capability Statement shall be comprised of the below information: 1. Brief History of the company. 2. Experience in delivering same or similar services/supplies. This section shall demonstrate the offer's experience and ability to provide skilled personnel and manage requirements that are the same or similar to those addressed in the project description or PWS. 3. List of current or previous contracts: The offeror shall provide contract title, contract number, period of performance, dollar amount, and description of work performed on up to five Government contracts. List should be limited to work performed within the last five years and include reference name, email, and phone number. 4. General information: a. title: Palm Beach Harbor, South Jetty Rehabilitation 2026, Palm Beach County, Florida
description: The work consists of rehabilitation of the South Jetty at Palm Beach Harbor. Rehabilitation will require substantial moving and manipulation of both new and existing stones to obtain the required interlocking within the tolerances provided. Mobilization of equipment and the construction necessary to repair the jetty must be water-based and require the use of marine construction methods and equipment. Work on top of the jetty will be permitted. Land-based access to the project site will not be permitted. Rehabilitation also consists of concrete repairs to the South Jetty at Palm Beach Harbor as indicated on the drawings. Prior to work on the jetty, conduct a pre-construction benthic community survey on the jetty structure and any adjacent submerged areas that may be impacted by the Contractors operations. Complete any coral relocations required as a result of the benthic survey prior to jetty work. Field personnel conducting coral survey and transplantation activities must either be qualified relocation contractors by the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission or must provide documentation of having successfully conducted relocation of corals in Florida. The project will have an estimated period of performance of 330 calendar days after receipt of the Notice to Proceed (NTP). The stated time is inclusive of 60 calendar days to commence work and will be divided into base work and three options as follows: The Estimated Magnitude of construction is between $1,000,000.00 and $5,000,000.00The Invitation for Bid (IFB) will be issued on or about September 23, 2026 and bids will be due on or about October 23, 2026.THIS ACQUISITION REQUIRES THE USE OF COAST GUARD-CERTIFIED EQUIPMENT, The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code assigned to this procurement is 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction. description: UPDATE (2026-10-16): Clarification for Clause 52.208-9 Q: Can the Government please clarify if this AbilityOne requirement was utilized on the previous (current) contract? A: Yes, the previous (current) contract does include FAR Clause 52.208-9 and utilized AbilityOne requirements. Q: Will the Government please provide the supply usage (quantities purchased) from AbilityOne on the previous (current) contract over the last year? A: The Government does not track or maintain records of the specific supply usage (quantities purchased) by the contractor under the current contract. The contractor is responsible for estimating, purchasing, and managing their own supply inventory in compliance with the contract terms and FAR Clause 52.208-9. Q: Please confirm that only consumables (paper products, can liners) will need to be purchased through AbilityOne? A: If different, please clarify.In accordance with FAR Clause 52.208-9, the Contractor shall purchase any supplies required for Government use under this contract from the AbilityOne Procurement List, provided they are available. Respondents will not be notified of the results and the U.S. Government is not required to answer any questions submitted in regards to this notice. Sources Sought Submission Requirements: It is requested that interested businesses submit information outlining their company information, small business standing, ability to perform in accordance with the draft Performance Work Statement (PWS), and intent of subcontracting. Submission is not a prerequisite to any potential future offerings, but participation will assist the Government in tailoring the requirement to be consistent with industry. Responses should reference the Sources Sought Notice and shall include the following information in this format: (a) Company profile including number of employees, office location, Unique Entity ID, and CAGE Code. (b) Point of contact, telephone number, fax number, address, and email address (if available). (c) Corporate Experience and Management: Global Operations: Describe your company�s experience managing logistics and warehouse operations of similar size, scope, and complexity across multiple, geographically dispersed international locations as detailed in draft PWS Section 1.1. How do you ensure standardized performance and quality control across all sites? Key Personnel: The draft PWS identifies numerous key personnel with specific, high-level qualifications (PWS Section 3.20). Describe your strategy for recruiting, hiring, and retaining personnel who meet these stringent requirements for the life of the contract. What is your plan for rapidly filling vacancies to meet the 30-day requirement? Subcontractor Management: If applicable, describe your experience managing subcontractors to meet the requirements of a complex, global contract. How do you ensure subcontractors adhere to all performance, security, and quality standards outlined in the draft PWS? (d) Technical and Operational Capability: Inventory Management and Accuracy: The PWS requires maintaining a 98% inventory accuracy rate and conducting 100% annual inventories (PWS Section 3.2, 3.6). Describe your technical approach and quality control processes for achieving and sustaining this level of accuracy across the estimated workload, including your methodology for causative research of gains and losses. Describe your experience in cleansing, normalizing, and standardizing large, disparate inventory data sets. Detail your capabilities and past performance in developing and integrating custom modules (e.g., material visibility, stowage optimization) with existing government or commercial Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems. Special Material Handling: This contract requires handling, stowing, and transporting various special materials, including Hazardous Material (HAZMAT), temperature-controlled items, and Security Risk Category (SRC) II-IV Small Arms (PWS Sections 3.2, 3.3). Please describe your experience, certifications, and established procedures for managing these materials in compliance with all cited regulations. Describe your plan and capabilities for rapidly augmenting your workforce and resources to meet these demands at any of the specified global locations. Describe your company's experience in managing cleared contracts and personnel, including your processes for ensuring compliance with all security requirements outlined in PWS section 3.17, particularly the unique staffing requirements for South Korea. Provide contract numbers, dollar value, and the period of performance for each contract referenced in the response to this source sought notice. title: Commercial Total Lightning (TL) Data Feed
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE End User: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), National Weather Service (NWS) Requirement: Commercial Total Lightning (TL) Data Feed NAICS Code: 518210 � Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services ($40.0M Small Business Size Standard) 1. DISCLAIMER & GENERAL INFORMATION This Sources Sought Notice is issued solely for market research, information, and planning purposes in accordance with FAR Part 10. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), or a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. The NWS is not seeking proposals or quotes at this time and will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in responding to this notice. Responses will be used by the NWS to evaluate potential sources, determine levels of competition, and assess set-aside opportunities under GSA Multiple Award Schedules or open-market commercial procedures. 2. REQUIREMENT SUMMARY The NWS requires continuous, real-time commercial Total Lightning (TL) data delivered via automated electronic data streams (AES-128 binary encrypted). The total lightning dataset includes both Cloud Flash (CF / In-Cloud / Intra-Cloud / Cloud-to-Air) and Cloud-to-Ground (CG) lightning events. The feed must directly ingest into NWS operational decision-support infrastructure managed by NWS Central Processing, including the Advanced Weather Interactive Processing System (AWIPS), Centralized Integrated Real-Time Repository for Unified Services (CIRRUS), and Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor (MRMS) models to support severe weather warning operations, Aviation Weather Center (AWC) corridor tracking, Storm Prediction Center (SPC) Lightning Jump algorithms, and Incident Meteorologist fire weather operations. Key operational requirements include: Scope & Event Classification: Real-time detection and classification of Total Lightning (TL) including Cloud Flashes (CF) and Cloud-to-Ground (CG) events. CF pulses/events must define vertical and horizontal extent (including estimated In-Cloud height up to 20 km with ~500 m accuracy) to evaluate convective potential. Probability of false flash type identification shall not exceed 20%, with no more than 2% false detections from non-lightning causes. Technical Performance Metrics: Location Accuracy: 2 km for 99% of the area within the designated geographic coverage zone. Timing Accuracy: Reported to 0.001 seconds (milliseconds) or better (UTC with microsecond resolution desired for event/pulse timestamps). Detection Efficiency: 60% or higher for over 90% of the 48 contiguous states; >50% over Hawaii and southern Alaska. Telemetry Data: Polarity (positive/negative), peak current in amperes for CG or peak radiated field normalized to 30 km for IC lightning, stroke/pulse count per flash (multiplicity), IC height in kilometers, and number of sensors utilized (5 to 25 sensors). Delivery & Archiving Standards: Continuous Secure Shell TCP/IP streaming data and 1-minute encrypted combination packets (AES-128 binary) containing flash and pulse sub-packets delivered to the NWS Telecommunications Gateway (NWSTG) within 1 minute or less of detection for dissemination over NOAAPORT/SBN. Level I streaming data must be made available for archiving at the National Centers for Environmental Information (NCEI) and NWS Meteorological Development Laboratory (MDL). 3. RESPONSE REQUIREMENTS Interested vendors capable of meeting the attached draft Statement of Work (SOW) are requested to submit a concise Capability Statement (maximum 5 pages) providing the following: Company Profile: Company Name, Address, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), CAGE Code, GSA Schedule Contract Number (if applicable), Business Size/Socioeconomic Status under NAICS 518210, and Primary Point of Contact (Name, Title, Email, Phone). Technical Capabilities: A detailed description of your commercial ground-based lightning detection network, broad-spectrum/high-frequency sensing methods, pulse/event grouping algorithms, spatial location and IC height accuracy metrics, and delivery protocols for continuous real-time TL data streams. Operational Experience: Summary of relevant federal or commercial contracts delivering real-time broad-spectrum total lightning feeds into severe weather decision-support systems, aviation corridor tracking platforms, or automated severe storm prediction algorithms. Market Feedback: Identification of any technical challenges, operational risks, or recommendations regarding the draft SOW requirements or NAICS classification. Submissions must be delivered electronically in PDF or Microsoft Word format to Paul Thomas at paul.thomas@noaa.gov no later than October 23, 2026 at 1300 hours ET. All proprietary, confidential, or sensitive trade secret data included in submissions must be clearly marked. The Government will protect properly marked proprietary information from unauthorized disclosure in accordance with statutory regulations.

title: Construction of Chilled Water Plant and Site Utility Upgrades at VA Medical Center in West Haven, CT
description: The scope of the chilled water plant replacement consists of the demolition of the existing chilled water plant (building 16a) and construction of a new multi-story chilled water plant to include chillers, cooling towers, pumps, and all associated mechanical and electrical equipment. Due to the close proximity of the existing fuel tank farm adjacent to the existing chilled water plant, a new fuel tank farm will need to be constructed as part of the project, which primarily serves the central boiler plant, requiring close coordination with the medical center and ongoing related projects.The scope of the site utility upgrades consists of the replacement and upgrade of the existing fire protection water main and the domestic water main from Campbell Avenue to Building 15. Site utility upgrades also include providing utility main loops of chilled water supply and return, steam supply, condensate return, domestic water supply, and fire protection water supply which will originate from the new chilled water plant and back-feed to Building 1. The work also includes the installation of redundant electrical feeder from the utility demarcation point to Building 19 and coordination with the local electrical utility provider to provide further electrical redundancy offsite as well. In addition, new water storage tanks will be constructed. This project involves civil/site, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, structural, geotechnical, and architectural disciplines. The project must also comply with the DVAs Physical Security Resiliency Design Requirements (PSRDM). It is expected that the chilled water plant will be constructed to meet USGBC LEED Silver certification. The work is located adjacent to and within an active Medical Center campus which will be operational at all times. Impact to on-going operations must be kept to a minimum and carefully coordinated with the Contracting Officer and VAMC staff. In addition, the work area is constrained due to the active medical center operations which will limit laydown and storage areas during construction.

title: Palm Beach Harbor, South Jetty Rehabilitation 2026, Palm Beach County, Florida
description: The work consists of rehabilitation of the South Jetty at Palm Beach Harbor. Rehabilitation will require substantial moving and manipulation of both new and existing stones to obtain the required interlocking within the tolerances provided. Mobilization of equipment and the construction necessary to repair the jetty must be water-based and require the use of marine construction methods and equipment. Work on top of the jetty will be permitted. Land-based access to the project site will not be permitted. Rehabilitation also consists of concrete repairs to the South Jetty at Palm Beach Harbor as indicated on the drawings. Prior to work on the jetty, conduct a pre-construction benthic community survey on the jetty structure and any adjacent submerged areas that may be impacted by the Contractors operations. Complete any coral relocations required as a result of the benthic survey prior to jetty work. Field personnel conducting coral survey and transplantation activities must either be qualified relocation contractors by the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission or must provide documentation of having successfully conducted relocation of corals in Florida. The project will have an estimated period of performance of 330 calendar days after receipt of the Notice to Proceed (NTP). The stated time is inclusive of 60 calendar days to commence work and will be divided into base work and three options as follows: The Estimated Magnitude of construction is between $1,000,000.00 and $5,000,000.00The Invitation for Bid (IFB) will be issued on or about September 23, 2026 and bids will be due on or about October 23, 2026.THIS ACQUISITION REQUIRES THE USE OF COAST GUARD-CERTIFIED EQUIPMENT, The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code assigned to this procurement is 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction. title: USACE SPK DBB Construction - Sacramento River East Levee Contract 5 (SREL C5), Sacramento, California
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE Project Description: SREL C5 Anticipated Posting Date: 07 October 2026 Sources Sought Number: W9123827X1CQR SAM Posting Title: USACE SPK DBB Construction � Sacramento River East Levee Contract 5 (SREL C5) � Sacramento, California SAM Posting Description: This Sources Sought Notice is being issued for market research purposes to determine the availability, capability, and interest of small business firms for a potential Government requirement. NO SOLICITATION IS AVAILABLE; requests for a solicitation will go unanswered. No award will be made from this Notice. Responses will be used to determine potential acquisition strategies, understand current market capabilities, and to gain knowledge of potential sources. GENERAL SCOPE: The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Sacramento District (SPK) anticipates a potential levee repair and remediation requirement located within the City of Sacramento, California, along segments of the Sacramento River East Levee (SREL) to the south of downtown Sacramento. The combined length of the levee segments to be remediated under this contract is approximately 0.4 miles. The Contractor must furnish all labor, material, equipment, quality control and supervision required to complete the work. The work includes, but is not limited to: providing and maintaining all temporary facilities; implementing stormwater pollution prevention plan requirements; complying with all applicable permit requirements and environmental mitigation measures; developing staging areas designated for Contractor's use to the extent needed; coordinating with Agencies and stakeholders as necessary; construction of seepage and stability berms and buried curb walls in various locations; researching, potholing, removing and replacing existing utilities; protecting existing utilities, reusing excavated soils that meet specification criteria for reuse as levee fill; importing soil for levee fill as necessary; managing and disposing of excess excavated soils; removing all temporary facilities; and restoring and vegetating all disturbed areas. The potential requirement may result in a firm-fixed-price solicitation issued approximately mid November 2026. If solicited, the Government intends to award the anticipated requirement by approximately mid-February 2027. The Government estimates that construction of the potential requirement can be completed within four hundred and eleven (411) calendar days from receipt of Notice to Proceed. If market conditions indicate this estimate may be unrealistic, Respondents are encouraged to provide specific information (such as known equipment lead times or other timeline concerns) for Government consideration when responding to this Sources Sought Notice. The Government currently estimates the magnitude of construction for the potential project is between $6,000,000 and $9,000,000. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for the potential requirement is anticipated to be 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction. The small business size standard for the NAICS, as established by the U.S. Small Business Administration, is $45,500,000 annual revenue / 1,000 employees. The Product Service Code for the potential requirement is anticipated to be Y1LC, Construction of Tunnels and Subsurface Structures. If there is a reasonable expectation that at least two (2) responsible small business concerns under this NAICS can provide the anticipated services at fair market prices, the Contracting Officer is required to set the acquisition aside for small business concerns. If competition is set-aside for small businesses, Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting, requires that the Prime Contractor will not pay more than 85 percent of the amount paid by the Government for contract performance, excluding the cost of materials, to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities. If no set aside is made, the requirement is competed with full and open competition, and the awarded Contractor is not a small business, the Contractor will be required to self-perform the percent of work identified in the solicitation under FAR 52.236-1, Performance of Work by the Contractor. Contractors with the skill, capabilities, workload capacity, and ability to obtain bonding to complete the project described above (either through self-performance and/or Subcontractor management) are invited to provide capability statements to the primary point of contact listed below. Other than small businesses are also encouraged to submit Capability Statements. CAPABILITY STATEMENT: Responses must be limited to ten (10) 8.5 x 11 inch pages with a minimum font size of point 10. Please provide the following information: 1) Company name, System for Award Management Unique Entity Identification number (SAM UEID) or Employer Identification Number (EIN), address, point of contact name, contact phone number, contact e-mail address, and statement identifying whether the company employs union or non-union workers. 2) Experience and capability to complete contracts of similar magnitude and complexity to the potential requirement, including at least three (3) examples of comparable work performed within the past six (6) years. Each example should include a brief description of the project, description of the work performed (identification of self-performance and/or Subcontractor management), customer name, customer satisfaction, timeliness of performance, dollar value of the project, and whether there were any challenges experienced during the project (delays, investigations, health and safety issues, labor shortages, management/organizational issues, etc.). 3) Business size and socioeconomic type for the applicable NAICS (ex: Woman-Owned Small Business, Serviced-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB), certified Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone), 8(a) Participant, small business, or other than small business (large business)). 4) Bonding capability (in the form of a Surety letter). Please submit all capabilities statements, information, brochures, and/or marketing material as one (1) document, limited to the page maximum above. Responses will not be considered an offer, proposal, or bid for any solicitation that may result from this Notice. Moreover, responses will not restrict the Government to an acquisition approach. This Notice is for information and planning purposes only. Respondents will not be notified of the results of any review conducted or the capability statements received. Please provide responses and/or questions by e-mail to the Contract Specialist, Jessica Padilla, at Jessica.Padilla@usace.army.mil by 1100 / 11:00 a.m. (PT) Friday, 23 October 2026. Please include the Sources Sought Notice number, �W9123827X1CQR�, in the e-mail subject line.

title: OCTET RH96 PREVENTIVE SERVICE PLAN FOR SARTORIUS OCTET INSTRUMENTS
description: This is a Notice of Intent (NOI). This notice is published in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 5.102(a)(1) requiring the dissemination of information regarding proposed contract actions. This is a Notice of Intent to award a sole source, firm-fixed-price purchase order under the authority of 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 5.101 and FAR 6.302�1, as only one responsible source is reasonably available. The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID), National Institutes of Health (NIH), intends to negotiate on an other than full and open competition basis with Sartorius Corporation, 545-1 Johnson Avenue, Bohemia, NY 11716, to provide verification services and a 12-month preventive service plan for three Sartorius Octet RH96 instruments. The equipment to be serviced consists of the following: Octet instrument Serial No. FB-70621 Octet instrument Serial No. FB-70620 Octet instrument Serial No. FB-70173 The requirement includes three Octet 2nd Hand Instrument Verification services and three Octet RH96 Preventive Service Plans. The verification service includes verification of required components, performance check, power-on check, review of device logs, software license check, and evaluation of potential issues with quotation for repairs. Upon successful completion of verification, the preventive service plan will provide twelve (12) months of coverage, including parts and labor for break/fix events, software upgrades where applicable, and two annual preventive maintenance visits. The period of performance is December 1, 2026 through November 30, 2027, once verifications are completed. Services shall be performed in Bethesda, Maryland, at the Vaccine Research Center. The Government requires OEM-authorized service support for these instruments. Sartorius uses factory-trained service engineers and application specialists and provides original spare parts, approved software support, and manufacturer-authorized maintenance procedures. As the original equipment manufacturer, Sartorius is uniquely qualified to perform the required verification, preventive maintenance, software support, and repair services necessary to maintain the instruments in optimal operating condition. Use of non-OEM service providers or non-original parts could compromise instrument performance, invalidate warranty or service coverage, and negatively affect the reliability and reproducibility of research data. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 811210, Other Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance, which has a size standard of $34.0 million. Sartorius Corporation is understood to be an other than small business. This will be the only notice of the Government�s intent to solicit, negotiate, and award to one source to satisfy this requirement. The Government plans to award a contract for this requirement within 30 days of this notice. While this synopsis does not constitute a solicitation, interested vendors may identify their interest and capability to satisfy this requirement. The Government understands that Sartorius Corporation is the only vendor that can provide the required OEM verification and preventive service support for these instruments. However, firms that believe they can provide the capability required to fully meet the Government�s requirement may submit a capability statement, including past performance, in writing to the identified point of contact within fifteen (15) days after publication of this notice. Such documentation shall be used solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct this procurement on a competitive basis. A determination not to compete this requirement, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. This notice does not obligate the Government to award a contract or otherwise pay for any information provided in response. The Government reserves the right to use information provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and legally appropriate. Any organization responding to this notice should ensure that its response is complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the Government to determine the organization�s qualifications to perform the work. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. For additional information or to submit responses, please contact Linda Smith, Contracting Officer at linda.smith2@nih.gov and Danielle Tines, Procurement Technician at danielle.tines@nih.gov.
